2610.07962.title: ReGraph: A Computational Account of Emergent Generalization in the "what" and "where" Dual Visual Streams
2610.07962.paper_summary: Where generalization capacity--the ability to extract context-invariant relational structures--first emerges remains a central question in AI and neuroscience. The foundation for this capacity lies upstream of the hippocampus, within the entorhinal cortex, where parallel pathways dissociate relational structure in the medial entorhinal cortex (MEC) from sensory content in the lateral entorhinal cortex. However, as Eichenbaum argued, such factorization likely originates earlier, driven by the segregation of the dorsal ('where') and ventral ('what') visual streams. Supporting this, grid-like firing patterns--a signature of MEC (context-invariant codes)--also appear in preceding neocortical regions along the dorsal pathway. Yet, how such representations are computationally formed along upstream pathways remains unknown. To investigate this in silico, we developed ReGraph, a recurrent dual-stream graph model with biological inductive biases, including retina-driven stream-specialized encoding, dorsal-to-ventral modulation, and dynamic lateral connectivity. Trained on the action benchmark Something-Something V2, ReGraph revealed a pathway-specific emergence of relational mapping: context-invariant codes and grid-like spatial bases uniquely co-emerged along the extended dorsal stream. In contrast, their absence in single-stream, unmodulated variants, and standard baselines implies that these inductive biases are prerequisites for relational structures. Crucially, our post-hoc analyses demonstrated that these grid-like bases serve as reusable routing templates for information processing via lateral connectivity. Together, our findings provide a computational account that generalization may not be a faculty that emerges abruptly within a dedicated region, but a property that already takes shape as sensory information is parsed into factorized streams of hierarchical visual processing.
2610.07962.paper_summary_zh: 一般化能力——提取上下文不變的關係結構的能力——首次出現的地方仍然是人工智慧和神經科學中的一個核心問題。這種能力的基礎位於海馬體上游的內嗅皮層，在那裡，平行通路將內側內嗅皮層（MEC）中的關係結構與外側內嗅皮層中的感官內容區分開來。然而，正如Eichenbaum所辯稱，這種因子化可能源於更早的階段，受到背側（“在哪裡”）和腹側（“什麼”）視覺通路分離的驅動。支持這一點的是，網格狀的放電模式——MEC的特徵（上下文不變的編碼）——也出現在沿著背側通路的前額皮層區域。然而，這些表示如何在上游通路中計算形成仍然未知。為了在計算上探討這一點，我們開發了ReGraph，一種具有生物學歸納偏差的遞歸雙通路圖模型，包括由視網膜驅動的流專門編碼、背側到腹側的調制和動態側向連接。在行動基準Something-Something V2上進行訓練後，ReGraph揭示了關係映射的通路特異性出現：上下文不變的編碼和網格狀的空間基底在延伸的背側通路上獨特地共同出現。相反，它們在單一通路、未調制變體和標準基線中的缺失意味著這些歸納偏差是關係結構的前提條件。關鍵是，我們的事後分析表明，這些網格狀基底作為信息處理的可重用路由模板，通過側向連接進行處理。總體而言，我們的發現提供了一種計算解釋，即一般化可能不是在專門區域內突然出現的能力，而是隨著感官信息被解析為分解的層次視覺處理流而已經形成的一種特性。
